Redshift Overview
• 	Redshift is based on PostgreSQL, but 	it’s not used for OLTP
• 	It’s OLAP 	– 	online analytical processing (analytics and data warehousing)
• 	10x better performance than other data warehouses, scale to PBs of data
• 	Columnar 	storage of data (instead of row based) & parallel query engine
• 	Two modes: Provisioned cluster or Serverless cluster
• 	Has a SQL interface for performing the queries
• 	BI tools such as Amazon 	Quicksight 	or Tableau integrate with it
• 	vs Athena: 	faster queries / joins / aggregations thanks to indexes

content.summary:
## Querying a data lake without a warehouse cluster

Athena queries supported data in S3 using a serverless query model; data layout and bytes scanned matter. Redshift is a managed warehouse family for sustained analytical workloads with warehouse-oriented performance and data modeling.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

Athena matches occasional SQL over S3 data without a managed cluster. Columnar storage and partition filters reduce scanned data. A warehouse may make sense for different sustained workload requirements, but is not necessary merely to run these occasional queries.

### Avoid this trap

Serverless querying is not free of layout decisions. Repeatedly scanning unpartitioned raw files can be costly; use appropriate columnar formats and partition pruning.

### Apply it

Analysts occasionally query partitioned Parquet logs already in S3 and want minimal infrastructure management. Which approach is the direct fit?

**Recommended design:** Use Athena with an appropriate catalog and partition-aware queries.

Athena matches occasional SQL over S3 data without a managed cluster. Columnar storage and partition filters reduce scanned data. A warehouse may make sense for different sustained workload requirements, but is not necessary merely to run these occasional queries.

quiz.question: Analysts occasionally query partitioned Parquet logs already in S3 and want minimal infrastructure management. Which approach is the direct fit?
options: Use Athena with an appropriate catalog and partition-aware queries.
Launch a permanent self-managed relational database solely to load every log before occasional queries.
Use SQS to execute SQL directly over retained S3 files.
Use CloudFront cache invalidations as a substitute for an analytical query engine.

## Stream ingestion versus processing

Kinesis Data Streams supports custom consumers and replay within retention. Amazon Data Firehose manages buffered delivery to supported destinations and can perform configured transformations; choose based on control, latency and destination needs.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

Firehose addresses managed destination delivery. Buffer settings affect freshness and cost, while backup/error handling protects failed transformations or deliveries. A replay-heavy multi-consumer design would justify evaluating a stream instead.

### Avoid this trap

A delivery buffer is not an arbitrary long-retention event log. A data stream is not automatically a complete data-lake storage and transformation pipeline.

### Apply it

A team wants low-operations buffered delivery of application events into S3 and does not need custom replay consumers. Which service is a reasonable starting point?

**Recommended design:** Use Amazon Data Firehose with an S3 destination and suitable buffering and error handling.

Firehose addresses managed destination delivery. Buffer settings affect freshness and cost, while backup/error handling protects failed transformations or deliveries. A replay-heavy multi-consumer design would justify evaluating a stream instead.
